newEntriesNeeded.title: NETGRIDCONTROL and NETDATASOURCE for Excel/CSV data import
newEntriesNeeded.principle: Use NETGRIDCONTROL with NETDATASOURCE to import spreadsheet data into PML macros. GridControl add-in must be imported before use.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Always import 'GridControl' with error handling before creating NETGRIDCONTROL instances.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- Import Excel data into PML
import 'GridControl'
handle any
endhandle
using namespace |Aveva.Core.Presentation|
!dataTable = object NETGRIDCONTROL()
!dataSource = object NETDATASOURCE('Grid Table', !filePath)
!dataTable.bindToDataSource(!dataSource)
!data = !dataTable.getrows()
!heading = !dataTable.gettitles()
pitfalls: GridControl add-in must be installed and accessible in the AVEVA environment
NETDATASource constructor varies by add-in version

newEntriesNeeded.title: CREATEELEMENT and ELEMENTTYPE for programmatic element creation
newEntriesNeeded.principle: Use CREATEELEMENT to create new PDMS/E3D elements programmatically. Set the element type via ELEMENTTYPE or SetElementTypeByName before adding attributes and executing.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Always validate ELEMENTTYPE before calling SetElementTypeByName. Check GetErrors() after Execute().
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
!elem = object CREATEELEMENT()
!etype = object ELEMENTTYPE('|<typeName>|')
if (!etype.valid()) then
  !elem.SetElementTypeByName('|<typeName>|')
  !elem.AddAttributeValue('|NAME|', !name)
  !elem.Execute()
  !errors = !elem.GetErrors()
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
!elementNet = object CREATEELEMENT()
!etype = object ELEMENTTYPE('|$!<class>|)
if (!etype.valid()) then
  !elementNet.SetElementTypeByName('|$!<class>|)
  !elementNet.AddAttributeValue(|NAME|, !tagName)
  !elementNet.Execute()
  !errors = !elementNet.GetErrors()
  do !error values !errors
    !msg = |$!tag;$!error|
  enddo
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
!elem = object CREATEELEMENT()
!elem.AddAttributeValue('|NAME|', !name)
!elem.Execute()  -- No element type set
pitfalls: ELEMENTTYPE must match a valid AVEVA class name
SetElementTypeByName by string name is more forgiving than ELEMENTTYPE constructor
GetErrors() returns an array that must be iterated

newEntriesNeeded.title: Chained STRING methods: replace().trim(), findfirst(), lowcase()
newEntriesNeeded.principle: STRING objects support method chaining in PML2. Common patterns include replace().trim() for data cleaning and findfirst() for array searching.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Chain .replace().trim() for cleaning input strings. Use .findfirst() to search ARRAY of strings.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern: !tag = trim(!row[!nameId])  -- trim is method, not function
pitfalls: findfirst returns an index value, not a boolean — use .set() to test validity
replace takes two pipe-delimited strings: search pattern and replacement
lowcase() returns a copy, does not modify in place

newEntriesNeeded.title: Nested handle blocks and scoping in PML
newEntriesNeeded.principle: PML handle blocks can be nested. Inner handle blocks take precedence for errors within their scope. elsehandle must match its corresponding handle.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Each handle must have a matching endhandle. Nested handles should be clearly indented. elsehandle none catches no errors (acts as pass-through).
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
handle any
  -- operations that may fail
  handle any
    -- inner operations
  endhandle
elsehandle none
  -- inner failure recovery
endhandle
endhandle
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
handle any
  !elem = object CREATEELEMENT()
  if (!etype.valid()) then
    !elem.SetElementTypeByName('|TYPE|')
  else
    !msg = |Error: invalid type|
  endif
endhandle
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
handle any
  !elem = object CREATEELEMENT()  -- missing endhandle
elsehandle any  -- orphaned elsehandle
pitfalls: elsehandle none catches zero errors — it is not the same as elsehandle any
Nested handle scoping can be confusing — prefer flattening when possible
Using namespace inside handle block may not persist after handle ends

newEntriesNeeded.title: FINISH directive to terminate macro execution
newEntriesNeeded.principle: FINISH is a macro directive that immediately terminates execution of the current macro. It is the equivalent of exit in a form context.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use FINISH at the end of macros that have completed their work or encountered a fatal error.
pitfalls: FINISH terminates the entire macro, not just the current block
Do not use FINISH in form methods — use RETURN or exit instead
FINISH is macro-specific, not available in all PML contexts
